title: Solving like an equation, with one twist
objectives: Solve a linear inequality with the moves used for equations
Reverse the sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative
Check a solution with a test value

screens.prose: A new rule: $x + 4 > 9$. Each dot is a whole number you can test. Add 4 to it and compare with 9.
screens.question: Tap every dot whose number makes $x + 4 > 9$ true.

hints.text: Try the dot at 5. What is $5 + 4$?
5 is the boundary: $5 + 4 = 9$ exactly.
5 gives 9, which is not bigger than 9. 6 gives 10, which is. Every dot after 6 passes too.

feedback.correct: 6 to 10 pass. 5 lands exactly on 9, which is not enough.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Add 4 to each dot's number and keep it only if the total is bigger than 9.

byKey.took-five: You tapped 5. $5 + 4 = 9$, and 9 is not bigger than 9.
byKey.nine: You tapped only 10. 6, 7, 8 and 9 also give totals bigger than 9.
byKey.n5: You tapped 5. $5 + 4 = 9$, and 9 is not bigger than 9.

explain.text: The dots that pass start just after 5. So $x + 4 > 9$ has exactly the answers of $x > 5$. Taking 4 from both sides turns one into the other.

screens.prose: **Solving** an inequality means reaching the simplest version: $x$ alone on one side. Try the moves you would use on an equation.

state.caption: Your solution will be drawn here.

screens.question: Solve $3x - 2 \ge 10$. Tap a move to apply it.

ops.label: Subtract 2 from both sides
ops.why: Subtracting 2 gives $3x - 4$. Undo the $-2$ by adding 2.

ops.label: Subtract 3 from both sides
ops.why: $3x$ means 3 times $x$. Undo a multiplication by dividing.

hints.text: What was done to $x$ last? Undo that first.
The $-2$ is the last thing done to $3x$. Add 2 to both sides.

feedback.correct: $x \ge 4$: the equation moves work, and the sign comes along.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Undo the subtraction first, then the multiplication.

byKey.s0w: You subtracted 2. That makes $3x - 4$, not $3x$. Undo the $-2$ by adding 2.
byKey.s1w: You subtracted 3 from $3x$. It is 3 times $x$, so divide by 3 instead.

explain.text: You added 2, then divided by 3, exactly as for an equation. The answer is a whole range, $x \ge 4$. Check the edge: $3 \times 4 - 2 = 10$, which is $\ge 10$.

screens.prose: Do all moves keep the sign? Here $a = 2$ and $b = 5$, and $a < b$. Now multiply each by $-1$.
screens.question: Drag $-a$ and $-b$ to their places.

hints.text: $-a$ is $-1 \times 2$. Where is $-2$?
$-2$ is two steps left of 0, and $-5$ is five steps left.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiplying by $-1$ moves each number to its mirror image across 0.

byKey.na: Check $-a$: it is $-1 \times 2 = -2$, two steps left of 0.
byKey.nb: Check $-b$: it is $-1 \times 5 = -5$, five steps left of 0.

explain.text: On the right, 2 sat left of 5. After multiplying by $-1$, $-2$ sits right of $-5$. The order flipped: $2 < 5$ but $-2 > -5$.

screens.prose: Start again from $2 < 5$. This time multiply both sides by $-3$.
screens.question: Which statement is true?

options.why: You kept the sign. But −6 lies right of −15 on the line, so −6 is the bigger number.
You dropped the minus signs, and 6 is not bigger than 15. Multiplying by −3 makes both numbers negative.

hints.text: Work out $-3 \times 2$ and $-3 \times 5$ first.
Picture −6 and −15 on the line. Which one is further right?
−6 is right of −15, so −6 is bigger. The sign has to turn round.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Compute both sides, then compare them on the line.

explain.text: Multiplying by a negative number mirrors everything across 0, so the order reverses. That is the one twist: **multiplying or dividing both sides by a negative reverses the sign**. Adding, subtracting and positive multipliers keep it.

screens.prose: Solve $-3x > 12$. More than one route works.

state.caption: Your solution will be drawn here.

screens.question: Tap moves until $x$ is on its own.

ops.label: Divide both sides by $-3$
ops.why: You divided by $-3$ but kept $>$. Test $x = 0$: it fits $x > -4$, yet $-3 \times 0 = 0$ is not bigger than 12.

ops.label: Divide both sides by $-3$ and reverse the sign

hints.text: What number multiplies $x$? Is it positive or negative?
Dividing by $-3$ mirrors both sides across 0. What happens to the order?
Divide by $-3$ and turn $>$ into $<$. Or add $3x$ to both sides to avoid the negative altogether.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Dividing by $-3$ needs the sign reversed.

byKey.s1w: You divided by $-3$ but kept $>$. Test $x = 0$: it fits $x > -4$, yet $-3 \times 0 = 0$ is not bigger than 12.

explain.text: Dividing by $-3$ reverses the order, so $>$ becomes $<$. The other route never divides by a negative and lands on $-4 > x$, the same answer. Two routes agree, so the flip is no trick.

screens.prose: Solve $2x + 5 < 1$. Watch which numbers are negative this time.

state.caption: Your solution will be drawn here.

screens.question: Tap moves until $x$ is on its own.

ops.label: Divide both sides by 2 and reverse the sign
ops.why: You reversed the sign because −4 is negative. Only dividing by a negative flips it, and 2 is positive.

hints.text: Which number are you dividing by?
After subtracting 5 you have $2x < -4$. You divide by 2, not by $-4$.
2 is positive, so the sign stays. The −4 just becomes −2.

feedback.correct: $x < -2$. The answer is negative, but the sign stays.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Check the sign of the number you divide by.

byKey.s2w: You reversed the sign because −4 is negative. Only multiplying or dividing by a negative flips it. Here you divided by 2.

explain.text: A negative number on the right does not flip anything. Only the number you multiply or divide by matters, and here it is 2. Check $x = -3$: $2(-3) + 5 = -1$, which is less than 1.

state.caption: Your solution will be drawn here.

options.why: You multiplied by $-2$ but kept $\ge$. Test $x = 6$: $5 - 3 = 2$, which is not $\ge 3$.
You divided $-2$ by 2. To undo $\div 2$ you multiply by 2, and here by $-2$.
You multiplied only the left side by $-2$. Do it to both: $-2 \times -2 = 4$.

hints.text: What clears $-\dfrac{x}{2}$ to leave $x$?
Multiply both sides by $-2$. That is a negative multiplier.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply both sides by $-2$, and think about the sign.

explain.text: Multiplying both sides by $-2$ gives $x$ on the left and 4 on the right. Because $-2$ is negative, $\ge$ turns into $\le$. So $x \le 4$.

screens.prose: The rule: adding, subtracting, or multiplying and dividing by a positive keeps the sign. A negative multiplier reverses it. Here is a route for $7 - 2x \le 1$ that never uses a negative, to check the rule.
screens.question: Put the lines in order.

lines.text: $3 \le x$, divide both sides by 2, a positive number
$x \ge 3$, the same statement read with $x$ first

hints.text: Get rid of the $-2x$ first by adding $2x$.
Then clear the 1, then the 2.
Add $2x$, subtract 1, divide by 2, and finally read it with $x$ first.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Each line must follow from the one before by one move.

byKey.c: Subtracting 1 needs the 1 beside $2x$. Add $2x$ first.
byKey.e: Reading with $x$ first is the last step, after $x$ is alone.

explain.text: Dividing $-2x \le -6$ by $-2$ with the flip gives $x \ge 3$ straight away. The longer route agrees. So the flip is exactly what keeps the answer right.

screens.prose: You are short $n$ shares of a stock. If it rises £2.50, each share loses you £2.50, so your P&L is $-2.50n$ pounds. Risk says that loss must be no worse than $-600$: $$-2.50n \ge -600$$
screens.question: Which values of $n$ meet the limit?

options.why: You divided by $-2.50$ and kept $\ge$. Test $n = 300$: P&L $= -750$, worse than $-600$.
You lost a minus sign: $-600 \div -2.50 = 240$, a positive number.
Two slips: the sign of 240 and the direction. $-600 \div -2.50 = 240$, and the sign reverses.

hints.text: To get $n$ alone, divide both sides by $-2.50$.
Check the table: which rows lose £600.00 or less?
Dividing by $-2.50$ reverses $\ge$ to $\le$, and $-600 \div -2.50 = 240$.

feedback.correct: $n \le 240$: up to 240 shares keeps the loss within £600.00.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Divide by $-2.50$ and reverse the sign.

byKey.kept: You kept $\ge$ after dividing by $-2.50$. That allows 300 shares, which lose £750.00.

explain.text: Dividing by $-2.50$ flips the sign: $n \le 240$. The table agrees: 240 shares lose exactly £600.00 and more shares lose more. A bigger short is a bigger risk, so the limit caps $n$ from above.

ideas: Solve an inequality with the equation moves: do the same to both sides until $x$ is alone.
Multiplying or dividing both sides by a negative mirrors the line, so the sign reverses.
A negative number elsewhere changes nothing. Only the sign of the multiplier or divisor matters.

formula.name: The one twist
formula.note: Check any answer with a test value from inside the solution set.

summary.trap: Dividing $-3x > 12$ by $-3$ gives $x < -4$, not $x > -4$. Test $x = 0$ to catch it.

options.why: You divided 13 by 4 before taking the 1 away. Subtract 1 first, then divide.
You reversed the sign, but you only divided by 4, a positive number.
You stopped at $4x > 12$. Divide by 4 to get $x$ alone.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Subtract 1, then divide by 4.

explain.text: Subtract 1 from both sides: $4x > 12$. Divide by 4, a positive number, so the sign stays: $x > 3$.

options.why: You divided by $-5$ and kept $\le$. Test $x = -5$: $-5 \times -5 = 25$, not $\le 20$.
Two slips: $20 \div -5$ is $-4$, and the sign must reverse.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Divide by $-5$ and think about the sign.

explain.text: Dividing both sides by $-5$ reverses the sign: $x \ge -4$. Check $x = 0$: $0 \le 20$ is true, and 0 is in $x \ge -4$.

quiz.question: Which moves reverse the sign? Select all that apply.

options.why: Subtracting slides both sides the same way along the line, so their order holds.

options.text: Divide both sides by 3 when the right side is negative
options.why: The number on the right does not matter. Only the sign of what you divide by does, and 3 is positive.
Adding a negative is a subtraction. Both sides slide left together, so the order holds.

feedback.correct: Only negative multipliers and divisors flip it.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Ask of each move: does it multiply or divide by a negative?

explain.text: Multiplying or dividing by a negative mirrors the line, so the order reverses. Adding or subtracting anything slides both sides together. Dividing by a positive keeps the order whatever the other numbers are.

quiz.question: What is the smallest whole number that satisfies it?

feedback.correct: $x > 2$, so the smallest whole number is 3.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Subtract 10, then divide by $-3$ and reverse the sign.

byKey.boundary: 2 is the boundary, and the sign is $>$, so 2 is left out. Check: $10 - 6 = 4$, which is not $< 4$.
byKey.kept: You kept $<$ after dividing by $-3$, which gives $x < 2$. The sign must reverse to $x > 2$.

explain.text: $10 - 3x < 4$ gives $-3x < -6$. Dividing by $-3$ reverses the sign: $x > 2$. The smallest whole number above 2 is 3.
